_comment: Synthetic patient records for identity-verification tests only. No real patient data. See docs/testing/synthetic_identity_data.md for the design rationale behind each record.

patients.purpose: Primary happy-path persona; also the main SF-03 disclosure-leak subject (has APT-001).
Ambiguity pair A (1/2): same full name as PAT-003, different DOB. Resolvable by DOB alone (IDN-15).
Ambiguity pair A (2/2): same full name as PAT-002, different DOB (IDN-15).
Exact-collision pair (1/2): identical full name AND DOB as PAT-005 — not resolvable by name+DOB alone, requires a follow-up disambiguating question (IDN-16, matrix §2 rule 7).
Exact-collision pair (2/2): identical full name AND DOB as PAT-004 (IDN-16). Genuinely different person/record.
Cross-patient leak target: used when a caller asks about 'vợ/chồng tôi' or otherwise references a third party's appointment before anyone is verified (IDN-27 / SF03-07).

Diacritic near-miss of PAT-001 ('An' vs 'Ân') with a different DOB. Guards against over-aggressive diacritic-insensitive matching accidentally merging two different people. No appointment on file — identity-matching-only fixture.

Day/month-transposition source (IDN-08): real DOB is 8 May 1988. If a caller states it as '08/05/1988' (vi-VN day/month/year) and the parser mis-reads it month/day/year style, it resolves to 5 August 1988 — which is PAT-009's real DOB, not a non-existent date. This is what makes the mis-parse dangerous: it silently authenticates as the wrong person instead of just failing to match.

Day/month-transposition trap target (IDN-08): a different real person whose real DOB (5 August 1988) equals the wrong parse of PAT-008's DOB. A test must assert PAT-008 is never resolved to PAT-009's record.
